findings.source_quote: ἔπλησε τοὺς -οὐρανούς· ὡς καὶ τὸ φαινόμενον στερέωμα ἄστροις ἐκόσμησεν
findings.english_quote: filled the heavens. He also adorned the visible firmament with stars
findings.issue: The draft preserves the two actions but flattens their comparative relationship. “He also” represents καί without adequately representing ὡς: the filling of the heavens with angels and spirits is compared with the adornment of the visible firmament with stars. The disclosed printed hyphen is not the problem.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a comparison-explicit construction, such as “filled the heavens, just as he also adorned the visible firmament with stars.” This proposed revision requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ πῶς φυτὰ καὶ ζῷα πλάσσει καὶ ταῦτα διαφοραῖς ἀναριθμήτοις πάσῃ ἀκριβείᾳ συνεχῶς ἀποτελουμένη
findings.english_quote: and how that nature molds plants and animals, continually completing them with countless differences and complete precision.
findings.issue: The main text is defensible as a middle-agent interpretation, but the note does not adequately disclose the material voice and attachment alternatives. Feminine agreement can connect ἀποτελουμένη with φύσις; it does not by itself establish that nature actively completes the plants and animals. ἀποτελουμένη is formally middle/passive, allowing a passive interpretation in which nature is continually brought to completion. The draft also takes ταῦτα as the plants and animals rather than considering the adverbial καὶ ταῦτα construction, “and this too.” Calling the alternative merely a “looser attachment to the larger creative process” does not preserve these differences clearly enough.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to state that the main text understands ἀποτελουμένη as a transitive middle, with φύσις as subject and ταῦτα referring to the plants and animals, choosing this interpretation for continuity with πλάσσει. Preserve the alternative passive sense, “nature continually being brought to completion,” and explain that καὶ ταῦτα can instead qualify the preceding assertion as “and this too.” Retain the confirmed supplied wording; no print correction is required for this interpretive ambiguity. The revised note and any resulting textual change require fresh review.
